title: Clerical life: Celebrating the day of the dead
gist: Anglican priest Alice Goodman reflects on grave-visiting traditions in her Cambridgeshire parishes (the Wilbrahams, Six Mile Bottom, Fulbourn), compares them to All Souls candles in Poland, describes pragmatically bending diocesan churchyard rules (but not for a two-foot concrete poodle), and affirms her belief in bodily resurrection.

insights.claim: Goodman reports an established tradition in the Wilbrahams and Six Mile Bottom of visiting, tending and decorating family graves weekly, akin to the candle-lit churchyards she saw in Poland for All Souls.
insights.speaker: Alice Goodman
insights.so_what: Signals persistent rural attachment to place-based ritual in English villages.

insights.claim: The comfort of grave-tending depends on families staying in ancestral villages for generations, with room left for the next generation to tend new graves.
insights.speaker: Alice Goodman
insights.quote: Only let there be room for the next generation

insights.claim: Diocesan rules generally ban artificial flowers and toys on English churchyard graves, but Goodman tolerates them, and offerings of rum, whisky, sherry and Cadbury's, because strict enforcement would cause grief.
insights.speaker: Alice Goodman
insights.so_what: Illustrates discretion in institutional rule enforcement at local level.
insights.quote: Strict enforcement of the diocesan rules in this corner would cause a lot of grief.
insights.locator: Toys aren’t allowed in my parish

insights.claim: A nearly two-foot black concrete poodle placed by a grave is too big to overlook, and Goodman plans to impound it if not removed by month end.
insights.speaker: Alice Goodman
insights.locator: Toys aren’t allowed in my parish

insights.claim: Goodman believes bodies are indivisible from souls, which she says is why bodily resurrection of the dead is central to her faith, a faith that holds churchyards are not eternal but the buried are.
insights.speaker: Alice Goodman
insights.quote: I believe that bodies are indivisible from souls
insights.locator: I think of my parents’ graves
